dossier.public_summary: The dips alternate between nearly absent and very deep (531 ppm odd vs 1717 ppm even) at 5.7 sigma and the six transits have very different depths, including a near-zero transit in sector 76. This pattern with a V-shaped, poorly fitting grazing transit is typical of an eclipsing binary seen at twice the period, not a steady 2.7 Earth-radius planet. Depth changes even within the same data product confirm the signal is inconsistent for a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by ~3.2x at 5.7 sigma. Classic signature of an eclipsing binary at twice the reported period (28.8 d) rather than a planet at 14.4 d.

Depth is not stable within the same pipeline: sector 76 depth 10 +/- 178 ppm versus sector 77 depth 2236 +/- 200 ppm. A genuine planet should be steady; large intrinsic changes favor a blended/spotted binary contributing variable dilution.

reasons.why: Marginal secondary consistent with the brightening 7.018 but phase 0.256 and shallow secondary_over_bump 0.9566 show no circular orbit or clean single secondary. V-shaped, poor transit fit off central duration (ratio 0.7039) favors grazing stellar companion over a flat-bottomed planet.
